query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a ductile phase through alloying can enhance the integrity of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy while preserving its caloric performance.
generation.intervention: Addition of a ductile alloying element (e.g., Cu) to form a composite microstructure
generation.conditions: Applied magnetic field (up to 5 Tesla), pressure (up to 100 MPa), and temperature (between 250 K and 350 K)
generation.structural_mediator: Ductile phase dispersion within the high-entropy alloy matrix
generation.mechanism: The ductile phase acts as a crack-arrestor, enhancing the alloy's toughness and resistance to cracking under applied fields and pressure, while the high-entropy alloy matrix maintains its caloric response
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved load-bearing integrity and preserved caloric performance relative to the unchanged alloy
generation.baseline: As-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy without ductile phase addition
generation.boundary: Applied field: 0-5 Tesla, pressure: 0-100 MPa, temperature: 250-350 K
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount and distribution of the ductile phase, as well as potential interactions with the high-entropy alloy matrix, are unknown

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled comparison of the caloric response and mechanical integrity of the alloy with and without ductile phase addition, under applied field and pressure
measurements: Caloric response (e.g., adiabatic temperature change), mechanical integrity (e.g., compressive strength, toughness), microstructure analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with ductile phase addition exhibits significantly reduced caloric response or unchanged mechanical integrity compared to the baseline alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
